title: Python Mastery
blurb: From names and references to decorators, generators, the data model, typing, asyncio and CPython internals: the Python you need to read, write and defend in an interview.
sources: Goodrich, Tamassia & Goldwasser, Data Structures and Algorithms in Python, ch. 1-2
Matthes, Python Crash Course (3rd ed.), Parts I-II (topic coverage; all wording and examples original)
The Python Tutorial, Language Reference (Data Model) and Library Reference, docs.python.org/3

title: The Linux Command Line
blurb: From your first prompt to shell scripts, text pipelines and on-call debugging: the command line explained from the ground up, with Python problems that rebuild the classic tools.
sources: Shotts, The Linux Command Line (5th internet edition)
Original material on ssh, tmux, curl, jq, git, cron, systemd, GPUs and Docker

title: Git (Pro Git)
blurb: Git from first commit to object internals: branching, rebasing, remotes, GitHub flow, history surgery and rescue drills, with Python problems that rebuild the commit graph, diff, merge and reflog yourself.
sources: Chacon & Straub, Pro Git, 2nd edition (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0), chapters 1-10
Original material on team workflows, commit conventions and rescue scenarios

title: Practical Vim
blurb: Learn Vim as a small language of operators, motions and text objects: the dot command, modes, files, registers and macros, patterns and substitution, project tools, a real-world setup and a 14-day practice plan. Turn on Vim mode in the ⚙ settings menu and practise in every editor on this site.
sources: Drew Neil, Practical Vim, 2nd edition (Pragmatic Bookshelf)
Vim and Neovim built-in documentation (:help)

title: DSA Foundations (Goodrich)
blurb: The theory track: a chapter-by-chapter tour of Goodrich, Tamassia & Goldwasser - analysis, recursion, arrays, lists, trees, heaps, hashing, search trees, sorting, text, graphs and external memory - with runnable implementations and build-it-yourself exercises.
sources: Goodrich, Tamassia & Goldwasser, Data Structures and Algorithms in Python (Wiley, 2013), ch. 3-15

title: Patterns I — Arrays, Hashing & Two Pointers
blurb: The first two NeetCode roadmap patterns, taught properly: how to attack an interview problem, hash maps from the inside out, prefix sums and counting tricks, and every flavour of two pointers.
sources: Goodrich, Tamassia & Goldwasser, Data Structures and Algorithms in Python, ch. 5 (Array-Based Sequences)
Goodrich, Tamassia & Goldwasser, Data Structures and Algorithms in Python, ch. 10 (Maps and Hash Tables)
NeetCode roadmap (NeetCode 150 / 250)
CPython documentation and source notes on dict/set

title: Patterns II — Sliding Window, Stack & Binary Search
blurb: Three patterns that turn O(n²) and O(n) scans into O(n) and O(log n): sliding windows, (monotonic) stacks and deques, and binary search done right — including binary search on the answer.
sources: Goodrich, Tamassia & Goldwasser, Data Structures and Algorithms in Python — ch. 4.1.3 (binary search), ch. 5.3 (amortization), ch. 6 (stacks, queues, deques)
NeetCode 150 roadmap
Python docs: bisect, collections.deque

title: Patterns III — Linked Lists, Trees & Tries
blurb: Pointer surgery on linked lists, every flavour of tree traversal, binary search trees and tries — the node-based half of the NeetCode 150, with a judge that builds the lists and trees for you.
sources: Goodrich, Tamassia & Goldwasser, Data Structures and Algorithms in Python, ch. 7 (linked lists), ch. 8 (trees), ch. 11 (search trees), ch. 13.5 (tries)
NeetCode 150 (Linked List, Trees, Tries)

title: Patterns IV — Heaps, Backtracking & Graphs
blurb: Priority queues and the top-k / two-heap patterns, the backtracking template with pruning, and the full graph toolkit: DFS/BFS, topological sort, union-find, Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford, MSTs and Eulerian paths — with 58 judged NeetCode problems.
sources: Goodrich, Tamassia & Goldwasser, Data Structures and Algorithms in Python, ch. 9 (Priority Queues)
Goodrich, Tamassia & Goldwasser, Data Structures and Algorithms in Python, ch. 14 (Graph Algorithms)
NeetCode 150 roadmap

title: Patterns V — Dynamic Programming
blurb: From recursion trees to tables: the state / recurrence / base case / order / answer framework, then the NeetCode 1-D and 2-D DP problems plus knapsack, LIS, string, grid and interval DP.
sources: Goodrich, Tamassia & Goldwasser, Data Structures and Algorithms in Python, ch. 13.3 (Dynamic Programming)
NeetCode 150 roadmap — 1-D and 2-D Dynamic Programming

title: Patterns VI — Greedy, Intervals, Math & Bits
blurb: When the locally best move is globally right (and how to prove it), interval sweeps and meeting-room heaps, matrix and number-theory tricks, and bit manipulation with Python's unbounded integers.
sources: Goodrich, Tamassia & Goldwasser, Data Structures and Algorithms in Python — §4.4 (repeated squaring), §13.4.2 (the greedy method), ch. 14 (greedy graph algorithms)
Bryant & O'Hallaron, Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective — ch. 2 (bit-level operations, two's complement, integer arithmetic)
NeetCode 150

title: DSA in JavaScript
blurb: Solve the core NeetCode interview problems in JavaScript: the language details that trip people up (sorting, numbers, Map vs object, shift), the data structures JavaScript lacks (heap, deque, linked nodes), and runnable JS versions of every major pattern.

ECMAScript Language Specification (Array.prototype.sort, Number, BigInt, bitwise operators)
MDN Web Docs: Map, Set, Array, String, Number, BigInt, Math
Goodrich, Tamassia & Goldwasser, Data Structures and Algorithms in Python (heaps, graphs, chapters 9 and 14)
